node_definition.done_when: reckon/crew/placement.py occupying_the_reservation counts only the live pointers whose placed worker can still hold memory in the allocation. That is a pointer recording placement whose recorded worker or supervisor pid is alive, or whose run is still launching (no worker pid recorded yet, attempt started within the dispatch's launch window). A placed run whose worker has exited holds no seat, whatever its manifest says and whether or not it has been promoted. That covers a complete-but-unpromoted run, a blocked run awaiting resume, and a run waiting on an external condition with no live process. Liveness is read with the same process-liveness reader the live classifier uses (named at file and line in the manifest), not reimplemented. The docstring states the rule. The roster cap of 25 is unchanged. tests/test_the_roster_counts_live_placed_workers.py covers, in a temporary RECKON_HOME with recorded pids from a stub that is alive or has exited: 1, thirty placed pointers of which twenty six have exited workers and four are alive, and a further dispatch is admitted; 2, twenty five placed pointers with live workers, and a further dispatch is refused naming the cap; 3, a placed pointer still launching, which holds a seat; 4, unplaced pointers, which hold none. The declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest: restore counting every placed pointer, and case 1 is refused. The test files importing reckon.crew.placement or reckon.crew.dispatch's roster are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under $TMPDIR, and they add no failing id. No real scheduler verb runs. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Only reckon/crew/placement.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py (the roster refusal call site near _refuse_over_reservation_roster only) and the new test file change.
